title: Training crate: stepwise G1 env API (reset/step) in native Rust
description: Expose the 720-step rollout loop in fs-cmaes-viz-wasm/src/g1_walking.rs as a stepwise env: G1TrainEnv::reset(seed) -> Observation, step(action) -> (obs, reward_shaping, done, info). title: Regress: G1 walking flagship (v067 whole-body kernel) cannot keep standing prior upright past 250/720 steps
description:
The cmaesEngine.test.ts test "the shipped owner package executes every CMA family plus both robot flagships" expects the standing-only prior to survive >336 steps and the curriculum to complete 720 steps. With the v067 (whole-body, 30-link) kernel, the standing prior fails at step 250 ("base height") and the curriculum fails at step 283 ("base height") — both before the 264-step push-pulse start. v066 (16-link) passed at 512 steps ("base tilt" after the pulse). The v067 addition of arms/head/upper-body as kernel-posed dynamic bodies has destabilized the prior/curriculum.

User directive (priority): the robot must walk AS FAR AS POSSIBLE, AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE, AND AS STABLY AS POSSIBLE, with a MULTI-FACTOR OBJECTIVE OVER TIME. The current single-scalar rollup weights actuator work and slip too aggressively; it punishes a stabilizing prior that is doing small corrective work, so the prior falls early. The new objective should integrate per-step signals over the trajectory and expose (a) distance / time -> mean forward speed, (b) cumulative stability (tilt, slip, contact, impact) over time, and (c) survival duration, all without reward-hacking collapse.

Acceptance criteria:
- v067 G1 standing prior survives the disclosed pulse (steps 264–336) on the standard terrain-and-push config; target: completedSteps > 336 in the existing test.
- v67 G1 walking curriculum completes the full 720 steps (horizon) on the same config.
- v67 G1 5,040-D optimization still improves the curriculum baseline across multiple declared seeds without reward hacking.
- New multi-factor objective over time: the receipt exposes both per-step and trajectory-aggregated versions of (distance, speed vs target, stability — tilt/slip/contact/impact, work, push impulse, recovery, contact-schedule mismatch). The per-step signals drive a CMA-visible mean+penalty term so the optimizer cannot game a single rollup.
- Standing-prior baseline (no learning) achieves >1.0 m forward distance and >0.5 m/s mean forward speed over the 1.5 s horizon on the standard config.
- Curriculum mean (no learning) achieves >1.0 m forward distance and >0.5 m/s mean forward speed over the 1.5 s horizon.
- Optimized policy (5,040-D, default seed) improves over curriculum on the multi-factor objective across all three declared Philox seeds, with no per-seed cherry-picking.
- bun test passes the existing schema-7 G1 packet-adapter tests AND the end-to-end flagship test.
- typecheck, lint, build pass; desktop + mobile smoke passes with zero console/page/network errors.

Scope: kernel patch lives in /Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensim; this repo tracks the new artifacts and tests. Possible: new schema-8 (v068) for the per-step multi-factor signal.
